name: Localism in Hong Kong
summary: Hong Kong localism is a movement that treats Hong Kong as a distinct community whose institutions, Cantonese culture and way of life must be defended against mainland China, and which puts Hong Kong's own interests first. Strands range from Chin Wan's autonomous city-state to self-determination and open independence, with a nativist wing hostile to mainland immigration and parallel trading and a civic wing defining Hongkongers by values and citizenship. Many adherents scorn the pan-democrats' non-violent, China-focused approach, and radical groups favoured militant street action.
scope: The post-2008 localist movement as it emerged around the 2011 book On the Hong Kong City-State, Hong Kong Indigenous, Youngspiration, Civic Passion and the Hong Kong National Party, with the mainstream taken as the autonomist-to-independence camp that defends Hong Kong first. It excludes the pan-democrat camp and Demosisto's civic self-determination except where noted, and the pro-Beijing camp. Economic and social questions are mostly inferred because localists have no developed program on them.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Localists questioned Hong Kong's capitalist system and business-government collusion, yet Hong Kong's laissez-faire tradition runs through the milieu; adherents are split and sources are thin.

public-ownership.rationale: Sources record no stance on nationalising industries; the movement criticises business-government collusion but is not organised around ownership questions.

property-fundamental.rationale: Adherents oppose redevelopment that destroys local communities, but also defend Hong Kong's rule of law and property regime; no settled line is documented.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Localists see Beijing's state security reach as colonial control; Andy Chan complained of increased surveillance before his speech, so security-justified surveillance is rejected.

state-harmful.rationale: Localists want a Hong Kong city-state or autonomous state with its own institutions, so rejecting the state as such is inconsistent with their program.

empower-police-military.rationale: Localist groups clash with police and see the PLA garrison and police as instruments of Beijing; more power for them is strongly rejected.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: No localist source addresses sex work; adherents are split between conservative and liberal strands.

decide-locally.rationale: Autonomy and Hong Kong-first self-rule are the core of localism; Chin Wan's city-state plan calls for decisions to be taken in Hong Kong rather than Beijing.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Defending Cantonese, traditional characters and local customs against mainlandisation is central; Chin Wan wants British and restored Chinese culture blended and protected.

gradual-change.rationale: Hong Kong Indigenous called for a militant approach based on bravery and force, rejecting the pan-democrats' gentle approach, so incrementalism is disfavoured.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Opposition to mainland immigrants and one-way permit holders is central; Hong Kong Indigenous and Chin Wan treat the influx as the largest threat to local institutions.

free-trade.rationale: Localists attack parallel trading and mainland-driven economic dependence but come from a free-port city; no trade-policy line is documented.

nation-first.rationale: Hong Kong first is the slogan; Chin Wan advocates Hong Kong-first and Chan describes Hong Kong as a nation under threat; statement read for Hong Kong as the country.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Chan appealed to Britain and the US to help Hong Kong, but sources record no general view on intervention for human rights.

open-borders.rationale: Localism centres on restricting mainland entry; Hong Kong Indigenous called the influx an incursion, which is incompatible with open borders.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Hong Kong draws nuclear power from mainland Guangdong plants; localists have not made this a documented issue.

revolution-justified.rationale: Radical localists favoured militant clashes and Chin Wan urged militancy in 2014, but the mainstream stresses elections and self-determination; mild agreement.

experts-over-public.rationale: Civic localists place sovereignty in citizens (Chan: sovereignty must rest with the people), so elite expert rule is disfavoured.

central-planning.rationale: Localists identify central planning with Beijing's system and distrust it; no economic program is documented, so low confidence.

land-value-tax.rationale: Localists oppose property-developer power, which could favour land taxes, but no localist source mentions it.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Localists fight parallel trading, but Hong Kong is a free port and no tariff stance is documented.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Nothing in localism points to abolishing money; it is a nationalist and civic movement within capitalist Hong Kong.

one-party-rule.rationale: Localists reject Beijing's one-party rule as colonial; Chan calls China an empire and civic localists demand democracy.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Some groups seek a return to British rule, but as transition to independence rather than monarchist belief; Hong Kong localists do not advocate monarchy, so mild disagreement.

democracy-best.rationale: Civic localists tie sovereignty to democracy and Undergrad demands a democratic constitution; Chin Wan's strand is more ambivalent, so agreement not strong.

right-to-secede.rationale: Localists argue Hongkongers' right to self-determination and independence under the ICCPR; Chan says sovereignty must rest with the people.

natural-rulers.rationale: Civic localists define the community by citizenship and rights, not birth; the Chin Wan strand is ethnocultural but no natural-ruler claim is documented.

political-violence-never.rationale: Hong Kong Indigenous and Chin Wan endorsed militant clashes, though Chan and others say they do not advocate violent overthrow; so disagreement is moderate.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Chin Wan's strand defines Hong Kongers by Hua-hsia cultural difference, while civic localists define them by values and citizenship, so adherents split.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Hong Kong Indigenous uses indigenous language for local residents against newcomers, implying local authority over land, though this is not about pre-colonial peoples.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Localists see Hong Kong as a victim of Chinese colonialism and look to Britain for help, so they are not demanding reparations from Britain; mild disagreement.

civilizational-union.rationale: Localists reject union with the mainland, but Chin Wan's strand proposes a loose Chinese confederation of separate states, so adherents split.

limit-population.rationale: Population control is not a localist demand; they are concerned about immigration, not birth rates.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Localism is about sovereignty and identity; none of the sources take a view on speeding up technological disruption of institutions.

restore-past-order.rationale: Chin Wan seeks restored Chinese culture and a city-state blending British heritage, yet other strands are forward-looking; split.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Localists are pragmatic about tactics (electoral versus militant) but the sources record no general rule for judging policy by results.

direct-action.rationale: Nulled: the statement now asks whether direct action should replace electoral politics (reworded 2026-11-10, Codex review). This answer rested on direct action used alongside elections or on a mixed record, which does not support agreeing that it should replace them; its sources need re-reading against the new text.

reviewHistory.rationale: Hong Kong Indigenous and Chin Wan preferred militant action over pan-democratic gentleness, but localists also contested elections; moderate agreement.
reviewHistory.author: claude-sonnet-5-5

This answer rested on direct action used alongside elections or on a mixed record, which does not support agreeing that it should replace them; its sources need re-reading against the new text.

means-match-ends.rationale: Radicals defended militancy while others kept to elections, so the relation of means to ends is a live split rather than a position.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Nothing in localist sources aims at abolishing the division of labor; the movement defends a functioning city economy.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Localists blame business-government collusion, not profit per se, so Marxist exploitation theory is not their frame.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Localists reject Chinese Communist Party rule and demand democracy and popular sovereignty.

collective-farming.rationale: Collectivised farming is associated with the mainland regime localists reject.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Not part of the localist frame.

taxation-theft.rationale: Not a localist theme; Hong Kong's low-tax system is accepted and localists want welfare for locals.

harm-principle.rationale: No documented stance; adherents are mixed on liberal versus conservative views.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Localism asserts group claims (Hongkongers' right to self-determination and local resources), so rights belong to groups as well as individuals.

state-as-business.rationale: Localists complain of government-business collusion; treating governments as businesses is disfavoured.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Civic localists define community by values, and Edward Leung rejected birth-based definitions; no support for genetic claims is documented.

total-state.rationale: Localists denounce Beijing's totalising control over Hong Kong and stress freedoms and the rule of law.

national-rebirth.rationale: Chin Wan speaks of restoring Chinese culture and Hong Kong's rebirth as a city-state, though not framed as decadence; weak inference.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Localists describe themselves as victims of annexation by an expanding empire, and want a small independent or autonomous city.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Localism values law and civic institutions; feudal oaths are not part of it.

bound-labor.rationale: Binding farmers to land and lords is far outside localism's civic or ethnocultural program and contrary to Hong Kong's modern order.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Localists contest Beijing's official narratives of history and identity, but sources record no general theory of knowledge and power.

universal-morality.rationale: Civic localists cite universal values like freedom and rule of law, but others stress distinct Hong Kong culture; split.

revive-national-language.rationale: Localists defend Cantonese, which is already in daily use, so revival is not the issue.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Business-government collusion is a grievance, but sources give no localist position on democratic voting in firms.

school-vouchers.rationale: Localists opposed national education but no voucher stance is documented.

economic-freedom.rationale: Localists question Hong Kong's capitalist system while defending its freedoms; no consensus is documented.

rule-by-example.rationale: Rule of law is emphasised by civic localists; reliance on rulers' virtue echoes Confucian-style Beijing rhetoric.

national-self-determination.rationale: Localists claim Hongkongers constitute a nation with a right to govern itself; Youngspiration speaks of the "Hong Kong nation" and Chan of national sovereignty.

force-without-un.rationale: No documented stance; Hong Kong localists lack any military project.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Localism is not organised around epistemology; Chin Wan draws on Chinese religion while civic strands are secular, so adherents are split.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Hong Kong Nativism Power opposed cash handouts to non-permanent residents, and Hong Kong Indigenous complained of newcomers drawing on housing and schools; Undergrad would extend welfare to the civic community by membership.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Localists campaign to preserve local heritage and oppose redevelopment destroying communities.

dominated-front.rationale: Localists appeal to the West rather than joining a front against it, but dominated-country framing appears in Chan's colonial language; no documented position.

workers-nation.rationale: Localists organise by Hong Kong identity, not by class, and the idea of workers organising nationally is not part of their program.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Civic localists define community by values and Leung explicitly rejected birth-based exclusion; segregation law is alien to the movement.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Not a localist frame, though they say business and the government collude.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Localists treat mainland arrivals as eroding local identity; Leung says anyone sharing Hong Kong values, culture and institutions counts, implying expected adoption of local ways.

elite-replacement.rationale: Chin Wan likens the influx to a Beijing colonisation scheme, which resembles a deliberate-replacement idea, but this is policy-driven rather than a conspiracy by domestic elites; mixed so only mild disagreement.

national-mission.rationale: Localists seek self-protection not exporting their system.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Gender analysis is absent from the localist sources, and adherents range from conservative to liberal.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Localists accuse the government of collusion with business and pan-democrats of being ineffective; Chin Wan attacks mainstream politicians.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Eugenic discouragement of births is not found in localist sources and clashes with Hong Kong's civic and liberal-minded ethos.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: After Mong Kok and the 2016 prosecutions localists denounce police abuse and demand accountability; Chan calls Beijing's rule coercive.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Edward Leung is himself of mainland birth and defines Hongkongers by values; race-mixing is not a localist issue.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Civic localists speak of citizens' equal rights, though the nativist strand creates exclusions; mixed.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Localists describe mainland influx as a Beijing colonisation scheme and Chan calls China a colonial master, so they apply colonial language to settlement.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Not a Hong Kong matter, and no localist source supports it.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Not a localist idea and inconsistent with their anti-state-power stance.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Chan says democracy requires sovereignty to rest with the people, and advocates argue the Basic Law lacks legitimacy because Hongkongers were not consulted.

population-transfer.rationale: Hong Kong Indigenous wants fewer mainland arrivals but not expulsion of minorities, and civic localists reject exclusion; mild disagreement.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Militants clashed with police while Chan denies advocating violence; adherents are split.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: The social-Darwinist idea is not in localist sources; Chin Wan's cultural revival ideas are not framed as competition among peoples.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Hong Kong banned the National Party and disqualified localist candidates over independence views, which localists oppose as suppression of political parties.

vanguard-party.rationale: Localist groups are electoral and street organisations; Leninist vanguard parties belong to the Beijing system they reject.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Localists blame policy and immigration pressure, not population as such.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: The nativist strand fears that mainland influx erodes local cohesion and Chin Wan stresses Hong Kong's distinct culture; civic strands dissent, so moderate.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Not a localist demand; they want elections.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Localists are on the receiving end of national-security emergency powers and defend rights; strong disagreement.

party-controls-media.rationale: Localists oppose Beijing-style control over media; Chan faced censorship pressure and press freedom is among Hong Kong's distinctive values.

party-commands-army.rationale: Localists reject CCP authority and the PLA garrison as colonial.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Localist parties formed and split quickly, and sources record no doctrine about binding members to party decisions.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Chin Wan proposes only a loose Chinese confederation of separate states, so pooled sovereignty is rejected.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Localists distrust the Beijing-appointed chief executive and want democratic accountability.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Church governance has no connection to localist politics.

clerical-rule.rationale: No localist group proposes rule by religious scholars; the movement is civic or ethnocultural and demands popular sovereignty.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Localists reject unlimited leader tenure as a mainland pattern and want accountable democracy.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Chan asks Britain and the US for help, so localists do not reject Western ties; Hong Kong has no alliances itself.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Housing costs are a localist grievance but abolition of renting is not proposed.

people-in-arms.rationale: Opponents argue separatists lack combat force; localists have not proposed arming citizens, and Chan avoids violence.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Localists reject union with the mainland and Chin Wan wants separation; the statement as framed for Hong Kong and China is rejected.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: School sex education is not a localist theme, and the movement's views would follow adherents' wider social outlook.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Nativist localists want citizenship tied to local roots rather than easy residence; Chin Wan stresses ethnic descent while civic localists differ.

minority-language-support.rationale: Localists want Cantonese defended in schools and public life against Mandarin, effectively supporting a local language that Beijing treats as secondary.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Third-world debt cancellation lies outside a movement concerned with one wealthy city.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Localists put freedoms and self-rule above Beijing's stability-and-prosperity argument.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Localists demand genuine universal suffrage, including for the chief executive, and criticise Beijing-vetted selection.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Monetary governance is not a localist concern; Hong Kong's currency board is not contested in the sources.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Localists see Hong Kong as their own homeland but no territorial exchange for peace figures in their writing.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: The classification of the Soviet Union is a debate in Marxist circles that localist sources do not enter.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Chan says Hong Kong is being annexed by China and advocates argue the Joint Declaration and Basic Law lacked consent from Hongkongers.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Religious institutions' relation to the state is not a localist topic.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Localists demand a democratic executive but have not described a ceremonial head of state above party politics.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Localists reject Beijing's use of force or law to stop Hong Kong separating and hold self-determination is a right; they oppose force as response to secession.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Autonomists such as Chin Wan accept Hong Kong staying in China with its own system, while independence advocates such as the Hong Kong National Party reject it, so the strands split.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Localists reject Beijing's rule as colonial; no sacralisation of any ruler.

character-from-environment.rationale: Localists do not address nature versus nurture; Chin Wan's ethnic emphasis and civic strands' value-based identity pull in different directions.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Localists defend rule of law against arbitrary Beijing power.

space-expansion.rationale: Space policy is wholly outside localist concerns.

leader-cult.rationale: Localists see personality cult as the mainland's political style and reject it.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: A debate internal to Marxism-Leninism that localists, who reject the Communist Party, do not engage with.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Localists oppose Beijing's pan-Chinese claims and Chin Wan separates Hong Kongers from the Chinese nation; they make no territorial claims abroad.

women-must-cover.rationale: A dress mandate for women is not a localist idea and conflicts with the movement's emphasis on Hong Kong's freedoms.

common-currency.rationale: Localists defend the Hong Kong dollar and distinct economy; a shared currency with the mainland would be resisted.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Chin Wan stresses ethnic difference from other Chinese and localists reject union with the mainland even on cultural-ancestry grounds.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Autonomists seek self-governing cultural institutions within China while independence advocates want a state; adherents split.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Veg describes identity shifts driven by ideas and civic consciousness, not by production relations.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Localists defend Hong Kong's courts and rule of law against Beijing and its majority, so courts should constrain majorities.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: The movement stresses economic self-sufficiency for Hong Kong, but not a closed bloc with colonies.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Labor and environmental clauses in trade deals are absent from localist sources.

moral-incentives.rationale: Replacing material incentives with moral ones is a communist-era idea; localists defend Hong Kong's market economy against that model.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Hong Kong Indigenous embraced militancy, but sources record no insurrectionary foco doctrine, and some localists reject violence.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Localists opposed national education and want Hong Kong's own history taught; Veg describes resistance to state-prescribed Chinese nationhood.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Chan calls Beijing's rule colonial, and localists reject rule by a supposedly more advanced society.

patriotic-education.rationale: The 2012 anti-National Education protests resisted pupils being taught loyalty to the Chinese nation and flag; Veg documents this as a formative localist moment.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Racial preferences in admissions are an American debate, and localist sources do not translate it to Hong Kong.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Localists criticise Hong Kong's capitalist collusion but sources hold no thesis on capitalism's crises.

delink-world-market.rationale: Hong Kong's open economy depends on world markets; localists have no delinking program, though they stress self-sufficiency from the mainland.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: This Leninist thesis is outside localism, which has no theory of global class exploitation.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Advocates demand a public-drafted constitution after 2047 and rights guarantees, though no specific entrenchment language.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Advocates argue the Sino-British Joint Declaration lacked legitimacy because Hongkongers were excluded; this is a close parallel.

elective-rulers.rationale: Localists demand democratic selection of rulers and popular sovereignty, rejecting Beijing-appointed leaders.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Localists defend resisting rulers who break promises of autonomy and universal suffrage; militants did so in street action.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Localists want a democratic legislature with real power, not an executive-led system.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Animal ethics is not in localist sources, so adherents' views are unrecorded.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: The Gramscian hegemony thesis is not used in localist writing, though Beijing's cultural policies are criticised.

native-born-offices.rationale: Nativists want locals to hold power, and Chin Wan sees infiltration by mainlanders as a threat; Leung's civic definition (values, not birth) tempers it.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Not a localist theme; Hong Kong ceded to Britain was not a localist claim.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Hong Kong Indigenous and Nativism Power want local-born residents to lead over newcomers; "indigenous" is used in the New Territories sense, not pre-colonial peoples.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Constitutional anti-fascism is a European debate that localist sources do not enter.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: US historical controversy with no connection to Hong Kong localism.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Localists claim Western-influenced freedoms and rule of law as Hong Kong's own, rejecting Beijing's claim that Western institutions do not suit China.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Localists see the PLA as an instrument of Beijing and want civilian rule.

office-by-exam.rationale: Localists favour election of rulers, not exam-based posts.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Localists resist mainland influence in Hong Kong's economy, but sources record no policy on blocking foreign takeovers of strategic firms.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Divorce law is not a localist topic.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Representative democracy is demanded; budget control follows, though not directly documented.

single-official-language.rationale: Localists oppose expanding Mandarin at Cantonese's expense and defend Cantonese and written English and traditional characters.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Disparate-impact doctrine is an American debate that localist sources do not engage.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Parallel trading complaints concern overcrowding, not consumerism as such.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Localists oppose Beijing's armed or political coercion over Hong Kong's choices, and regard such intervention as colonial.

corporate-influence.rationale: Localists criticise collusion between business and government and developers' dominance of policy.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Hong Kong authorities use foreign-collusion rules against activists; localists appeal to Western help and oppose such limits.

residents-only-property.rationale: Localists complain of mainland buyers and resource competition and support protecting locals' access to housing and land.

democratic-peace.rationale: Democratic-peace theory is not cited by localists, though they do champion democracy.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Localist militants broke assembly laws and rejected Basic Law legitimacy, implying no general duty to obey; mixed because mainstream accept legal process.

non-intervention.rationale: Chan asks Britain and the US to intervene on Hong Kong's behalf, contradicting strict non-intervention.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Chin Wan frames Beijing's policy, not a minority, as the conspirator; no minority-conspiracy claim in sources.

local-production.rationale: Localists emphasise economic self-sufficiency and local resource protection, though not specifically local production.

informal-organisation.rationale: Localist groups formed small groups and parties alike, and some independents rejected parties; split.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Localists cite the ICCPR, which supports international law, but also assert Hong Kong's own constitution; split.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Localists seek economic self-sufficiency and Hong Kong-first policy so local revenue stays local.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: The personal versus productive property distinction is a socialist theme absent from localist sources.

defeat-communism.rationale: Chan calls China an empire threatening free peoples; localists treat CCP rule as the enemy, though not as a global crusade.

religion-illusion.rationale: Marxist religious critique is not a localist theme; adherents include both secular and Chin Wan's religion-inflected strand.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Localists question Hong Kong's capitalism but rely on its prosperity; no stance.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Localist sources have no feminist economic analysis.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Localists defend Hong Kong Cantonese and its English borrowings against mainland Mandarin; purging is not part of it.

treaties-binding.rationale: Advocates rely on the Joint Declaration and Basic Law promises being honoured, citing broken promises of universal suffrage.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Localists reject Beijing's communism but are ambivalent toward Hong Kong's capitalism, which they criticise for collusion; no third-way doctrine is stated.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Chin Wan stresses a historical Hong Kong identity but no land claim logic is documented.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Holocaust denial is absent from localist sources and incompatible with a movement that defends historical truth against official Beijing narratives.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Localists are themselves the targets of suppression and denounce it as colonial control.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Localists oppose restrictions on expression and no group seeks blasphemy laws.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Chan calls Beijing Hong Kong's colonial master and criticises extractive rule; localists reject this arrangement.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Islamic doctrine on jihad has no connection to Hong Kong localism.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Overthrowing rulers over religious law is foreign to localism, which seeks democratic and national self-rule.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Civic localists want citizens to decide Hong Kong's future directly, including through referendums on self-determination.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Chin Wan criticised left-leaning cosmopolitan activists; the framework is not part of localist thought.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Transgender legal recognition is not part of the localist program, and adherents' views vary.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Localists claim to move beyond the pan-democrat versus pro-Beijing camps and unite activists of varying views under Hong Kong-first.

alienated-labor.rationale: Marx's alienation thesis is not used in localist writing.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Chan locates sovereignty in the people.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Religious dress in state institutions is not a localist issue.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Workplace harassment settlements are not a localist concern.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Hong Kong has no army; Chin Wan's city-state vision has no discussed military policy.

rich-first.rationale: Deng Xiaoping's let-some-get-rich-first doctrine is a Beijing idea localists do not discuss; they criticise elite collusion but record no stance on it.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Chan appeals to Britain and the US, aligning Hong Kong with the West.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Localists demand elected rulers and popular sovereignty.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: IMF-style austerity is not a localist concern; Hong Kong is a creditor economy.

property-franchise.rationale: Localists demand universal suffrage and attack functional constituencies as unrepresentative.

reification.rationale: Lukacs's critique is not used in localist sources.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Rule of law is a core claimed Hong Kong value for civic localists against arbitrary Beijing power.

racial-franchise.rationale: Civic localists define the community by values and citizenship, and even ethnocultural strands do not propose racial voting restrictions.

online-participation.rationale: Localists organised online, but no documented stance on formal e-participation.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Restricting marriages by religion has no place in the localist program; adherents defend personal freedoms.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Hong Kong Indigenous targeted parallel traders' operations, not a religious minority; shop boycotts of a religious minority are alien to localism.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Localists attack tycoon and developer collusion with government, linking concentrated economic power to political capture.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Localists reject CCP-style state ideology promotion.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Localists denounce police violence, but want their own city-state institutions, not abolition.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Localists want welfare tied to the civic community, not charity-only.

term-limits.rationale: Anti-elite and democratic framing support term limits, not directly documented.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Existential-risk policy is not a localist concern.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Religious leadership roles for women are not a localist topic.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Localists oppose extending rights to non-permanent residents; Hong Kong Nativism Power opposed even cash handouts to them.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Localists mobilised through voluntary student groups and opposed state-run national education, so uniformed state youth movements are rejected.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Localists object to the PLA garrison and mainland presence; not a stand on foreign bases generally, but they seek no neutral demilitarisation either.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Chin Wan warns of cultural genocide and Tiananmen remembrance is a localist theme, though the statement is generic.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Localists criticise tycoon collusion but sources do not set out a labor-over-ownership principle.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Pacifism of this absolute kind is not a localist stance, and militant strands accept force in self-defence of the city.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Localists build identity on recent post-war Hong Kong civic history rather than ancient continuity, though Chin Wan stresses Chinese roots.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Queer-theory claims about sex are not in localist writing.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Jailed activists such as Edward Leung are honoured and the slogan became a symbol; localists honour sacrifice for Hong Kong.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Chin Wan draws on Chinese religion for warrior ideals, but other strands are secular, so adherents split.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Localists want a territorial Hong Kong nation for those living there, not a cultural centre for a scattered diaspora.

culture-before-state.rationale: Chin Wan puts cultural renewal and city-state building first, while independence advocates push political change first, so adherents split.

god-not-male.rationale: Theological language is not a localist concern.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Localists criticise mainland capital and traders' influence in Hong Kong, a mild preference for locals controlling the economy.

municipal-property.rationale: Municipal ownership of production is not in localist programs, though the city-state idea gives local communities a central role.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Chin Wan proposes a confederation of separate parallel Chinese states, with Hong Kong city-state as a unit; not communalist but confederal.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Drug regulation is not a localist concern.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Chin Wan stresses spiritual elements; others secular.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Localists reject Beijing's view that Hong Kong's autonomy is delegated and withdrawable; they demand genuine, guaranteed autonomy.

gm-crops.rationale: Crop biotechnology is not a localist issue.

racial-group-interests.rationale: The Chin Wan strand treats Hongkongers as an ethnic group with interests; civic localists reject ethnic framing.

racial-pride.rationale: The Chin Wan strand embraces ethnocultural pride, while civic localists stress shared values, so adherents split.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Localists distinguish Hongkongers from other Chinese speakers; shared language with the mainland does not make one nation.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Localists see Beijing as the threat and welcome foreign help.

free-public-college.rationale: Localists did not campaign for tuition-free universities in the sources consulted; student groups focused on democracy and identity.

capital-controls.rationale: Hong Kong's free capital flows are not challenged by localists.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Militants rejected police authority in street clashes but no stance on arms.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Mutiny against interstate wars is not in localist sources.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Global economic rules for developing countries are outside localist concerns.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Radical localists seek independence from the PRC state but not to smash Hong Kong's own institutions.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Chin Wan calls Beijing's policy neo-imperialist and colonisation, and Chan calls China Hong Kong's colonial master.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Localists emphasise Hong Kong's distinct identity, but the sources give no view on a universal human nature that grounds rights.

public-service-media.rationale: Localists defend press freedom against Beijing; public broadcaster independence is plausible but undocumented.

communal-electorates.rationale: Localists want one civic electorate for Hong Kong and oppose communal or functional-constituency divisions, so separate religious electorates have no place.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: No stated position; localists defended judicial independence and common-law protections, but no stance on fixed sentences.

voter-id.rationale: Nativist localists want tighter control of mainland arrivals but civic localists stress citizenship by values; no stated position on voter ID, so neutral.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Economic policy is mostly absent from localist platforms, so welfare design is treated as neutral.

race-social-construct.rationale: Nativist and civic strands differ on how Hongkongers are defined, and the movement does not address the scientific status of race, so neutral.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: No stated position; localists have no developed gender program and adherents differ.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Localists are hostile to the Chinese party-state and the Beijing line (s1, s6), which rules out defending its planned order.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Localists favour self-determination and a referendum on Hong Kong's future (s6, s1), which is a vote by inhabitants.

close-ties-china.rationale: Localists put Hong Kong first and resist economic and political dependence on the mainland, so they reject closer ties with China as a goal.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Localists have no developed welfare programme; the nativist wing wants benefits reserved for locals, which does not settle targeted versus universal provision.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Religious denomination is not a localist organising principle and the movement is split on how religion relates to politics.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Localists stress Cantonese culture and way of life, but the sources do not frame it as a technology versus tradition question.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Localists are defined by opposition to the Chinese Communist Party's rule over Hong Kong, so a market economy under party rule is rejected as the mainland model.

missingStatements.text: Immigration to a territory should be limited so that newcomers do not outnumber or crowd out the existing local population.
missingStatements.rationale: Hong Kong Indigenous and Nativism Power argue one-way permit holders dilute the local population and strain schools, housing and jobs; Chin Wan calls the influx a colonisation scheme.

missingStatements.text: A territory's native language should be protected in schools and public life against the spread of the dominant national language.
missingStatements.rationale: Localists defend Cantonese and traditional characters against Mandarin expansion as resistance to mainlandisation.

missingStatements.text: A people should be able to hold a referendum on its own political future, including sovereignty.
missingStatements.rationale: Demosisto proposed a referendum on Hong Kong's future after 2047, and ALLinHK planned to push for a self-determination referendum.

notes: Strands differ: Chin Wan's ethnocultural city-statism accepts Chinese confederation and opposes democratising China, while civic localists define Hongkongers by values and want democracy in Hong Kong; independence advocates and autonomists split on secession. Economic and social answers are largely inferred.
